en.title: ZipRecruiter OA #11: Lamps and Control Points
en.description: There are several lamps on a number line, each lighting a segment: lamp i covers the segment from lamps[i][0] to lamps[i][1] (inclusive). You are also given an array of control points points. For each control point points[j], find how many lamps light it, that is, the number of lamps for which points[j] lies within [lamps[i][0],lamps[i][1]]. Output the answers in control-point order.
en.input: The first line contains two integers n and m; then n lines follow, each with two integers l and r describing a lamp; the last line contains m integers points. 1≤n,m≤100000, −10^9≤l≤r≤10^9, −10^9≤points[j]≤10^9.
en.output: Output one line of m integers; the j-th is the number of lamps lighting points[j].
en.explanation:
Example 1: lamps [1,7], [5,11], [7,9]. Point 7 is lit by three lamps, point 1 by 1, point 5 by 2, point 10 by 1, point 9 by 2, and point 15 by none, so output 3 1 2 1 2 0.
Example 2: endpoints 2 and 4 are both lit, while 1 and 5 are not.
Example 3: both identical lamps [0,3] are counted.
hints: Point p is covered by [l,r] if and only if l≤p≤r.
Coverage = number of lamps with left endpoint ≤p − number of lamps with right endpoint <p.
Sort the left and right endpoints separately, then binary search.
